Wedding Invitation Wording: Formal, Casual and Digital Examples

Write a clear wedding invitation with wording examples for formal ceremonies, family celebrations and digital invites, plus an essential information checklist.

Wedding invitation wording needs to do two jobs: welcome guests and give them the details they need to attend. A beautiful design cannot replace a correct date, time, location and response instruction. Use this guide to choose a tone, write clear invitation text and organise the information for a printed or digital wedding invitation.

Wedding Invitations10 min readUpdated 17 November 2026

Decide who is inviting and what tone to use

Couple-hosted invitation

When the couple hosts, the message can speak directly in their own voice: “Together with our families, we invite you…” or “We would love you to join us as we get married.” Keep the language true to how the couple communicates.

Family-hosted invitation

If parents or family members are hosting, name the hosts clearly and state the couple’s names. Check family preferences before deciding whose names appear first or how traditions should be represented.

Formal or relaxed tone

Formal wording suits a traditional ceremony or formal reception; casual wording can be shorter and warmer. Both should still include the practical details in a consistent format.

The details guests need before the wedding

Core event information

Include the couple’s names, ceremony date, start time, venue name, full address and the parts of the celebration guests are invited to attend. If the reception is at another location, give a separate address and time.

Response and planning information

Add the RSVP deadline and the contact method. Where useful, explain dress code, parking, accessibility, child attendance, meal arrangements or transport. Avoid including private personal details or posting a home address on a public link.

Formal wedding invitation wording examples

Traditional family-hosted style

“[Host names] request the pleasure of your company at the marriage of [Name] and [Name] on [day], [date], at [time]. The ceremony will take place at [venue and address]. Kindly reply by [RSVP date] to [contact].”

Formal couple-hosted style

“With joy, [Name] and [Name] invite you to celebrate their wedding on [date] at [time] at [venue]. We would be honoured by your presence. Please respond by [RSVP date].”

Casual wedding invitation wording examples

Warm and simple

“We’re getting married! Please join [Name] and [Name] on [date] at [time] at [venue] for a ceremony, good food and a celebration with our favourite people. Let us know by [RSVP date].”

Small wedding or intimate gathering

“We’re keeping our celebration small and would love you to be part of it. Join us for our wedding on [date] at [time] at [venue]. Please reply to [contact] by [date].”

Write a digital wedding invitation page

Organise the page in a guest-friendly order

Start with the couple’s names and date. Put the ceremony and reception details near the top, then add a short welcome note, travel or dress guidance and RSVP instructions. Guests should not have to scroll through a long story to find the location.

Use the selected template’s real capabilities

A digital invitation can include images and a consistent visual theme. Wishly’s wedding and invitation collections offer ready-made starting points, but layouts and interactions vary. Check whether the chosen design has a response form; otherwise provide a separate reply contact.

Before you send the invitation link

Proofread like an event organiser

Verify every name, spelling, date, time zone, venue and contact. Ask another person to check the information, especially if multiple family members are hosting. Open the live page on a phone and test the map or buttons if the design includes them.

Keep guest privacy in mind

Send a private guest link where appropriate. Avoid publishing guest lists, phone numbers or details that should only be shared with invited people. Ask permission before showing photos of family members.

Wedding invitation checklist

The final checks

Couple names; host wording; ceremony date and time; venue and address; reception details; dress code if needed; RSVP deadline and contact; mobile preview; and a working published link.

Frequently asked questions

Should wedding invitations be written in first or third person?

Either can work. Couple-hosted invitations often use first person, while family-hosted or formal invitations may name the hosts. Choose one style and keep it consistent.

What information is essential on a wedding invitation?

At minimum, include the couple’s names, date, time, venue and address, which events guests are invited to, and a clear RSVP method and deadline.

Can a digital wedding invitation include RSVP?

It depends on the platform and the selected design. Wishly notes that interactions vary by template, so test the chosen template or provide a separate contact for responses.
